title: Hawkins hears Basie's band after hours; the buddha on the bandstand
summary: After hours Henderson's men hear Basie's band with its rocking buddha, and Hawkins is challenged by the Kansas City saxophone players including Herschel Evans.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Of course, in 1933. They played down at another big ballroom and Herschel had sat in the band, Les had sat in the band, but they had to go to work. After hours they went over to hear Basie's band. And when Fletcher walked in and when they walked in and heard that band and that buddha was moving, they said, 'My God, what is this?'

It was a buddha that they had on the bandstand, a buddha, you know, from China. It was a buddha that they had from a guy that built bandstands, a black man that built the most beautiful bandstands. This buddha was rocking and the whole band stood up there and I was with Bobby Stark and Dickie Wells was over here. Then I went down to the bar where Kingfish was - that's when -

Kingfish was the bartender. He's alive, thank God. Coleman Hawkins got a full glass of whiskey because Herschel played that night. This is the great night that's in the book of "Hear Me Talking to You". Ben said, "Kitten, come down here," and they weren't trying to outplay Hawk. They were just glad that Hawk was there, but Hawkins had never been challenged like this. He had never sit around with saxophone players like this.
With Herschel? Where was Herschel from, by the way?
